theme: Shapes make shapes: little shapes build big ones

activities.title: Two shapes hug
activities.intro: Little shapes can hug together and make a brand new shape. Listen to the story, then tap the shape they make.
activities.offScreen: Go get a cracker or a slice of bread, cut it corner to corner with a grown-up, and see what the two pieces can build.

rounds.prompt: Two triangles hug along their long sides. Which new shape do they make? Tap it.
A circle was cut right down the middle. The two halves hug back together. Which shape do they make? Tap it.
Two little blocks stack up, one on top of the other, and make one big tall block. Which shape do they make? Tap it.
Four little squares hug together, two on top and two on the bottom. Which big shape do they make? Tap it.

activities.title: Above, below, beside
activities.intro: Listen to where each thing is: above, below or beside. Then tap the one the question asks for.
activities.offScreen: Go stand beside a chair, hold a toy above your head, and hide a sock below the table, saying each word out loud as you go.

rounds.prompt: The bird flies above the flower. Tap the one that is above.
The star shines above the leaf, and the fish swims below the leaf. Tap the one that is below the leaf.
The block sits beside the cup. Tap the one that is beside the cup.
The star hangs above the cup, and the coin hides below the cup. Tap the one that is above the cup.

activities.title: Count the builders
activities.intro: A big shape got built from little ones. Count the little builders with your finger, then tap how many.
activities.offScreen: Go build one big square out of four little blocks and count each block out loud as you set it down.

rounds.prompt: How many triangles built the big square? Touch each triangle as you count, then tap the number.
How many squares built the big window? Touch each square as you count, then tap the number.
How many blocks built the tall tower? Touch each block as you count, then tap the number.
How many triangles built the pointy crown? Touch each triangle as you count, then tap the number.

parentCard.title: Cut-and-build shape pictures
steps: Draw one big square and one circle on stiff paper together, then cut the square corner to corner into two triangles, their hands on the scissors and yours close by.
Ask: can the two triangles hug to make a square? Let them turn and flip the pieces themselves until they do.
Cut the circle down the middle, mix the halves in with the triangles, and let them rebuild the circle.
Build one picture together from all the pieces, a boat or a house or a fish, and glue it down if they want to keep it.
Name positions while you build: the roof goes above, the door goes below, the window sits beside.
notice: When a piece does not fit, do they turn or flip it themselves, or put it down?
Do they use above, below or beside on their own while you build?
After the gluing, do they see a boat or a house, or still two triangles and a circle: what do they call it?
